capability: Put embedded Launcher payload admission inside the existing Application entry budget, bound descriptor and Bootstrap sizes, and defer Bootstrap content hashing and custody until Setup
searchEvidence: ManagedLauncherEntryCoordinator is the existing single owner of the monotonic local-entry budget, but the distribution host currently reads both embedded resources before RunAsync starts that budget.

EmbeddedManagedDistributionPayloadSource is the existing sole descriptor parser, Bootstrap payload inspector, exact capture owner and materializer byte-custody adapter; no second parser, updater or timer is required.

The prior executable ceiling was 80000000 bytes while the embedded Bootstrap identity and managed-setup payload schema accepted any positive size; the owner approved one explicit 200000000-byte Launcher/Bootstrap safety ceiling without making package size a release gate.

Existing host and infrastructure tests use preallocated byte arrays and therefore cannot prove bounded descriptor reads, zero healthy-path Bootstrap content reads, or a shared absolute 250 ms payload/state/root budget.
semanticOwner: VersionManagement Application owns one absolute entry deadline and typed payload admission result; VersionManagement Infrastructure remains the sole embedded descriptor parser, bounded resource reader, hash and exact byte-custody owner; Bootstrap remains composition wiring only
terminalContract: Every Launcher invocation begins one monotonic entry budget before payload admission. Healthy routing reads at most 65537 descriptor bytes, admits a Bootstrap no larger than 200000000 bytes by exact resource existence and declared length, and reads zero Bootstrap content bytes. Payload admission, state load and exact-root observation share the same 250 ms local-health cutoff. Only Setup inspection and capture stream, hash or retain Bootstrap content. The 200000000-byte Launcher/Bootstrap ceiling is allocation safety, not a package-size or optimization release gate. Missing or inaccessible resources return typed unavailable; malformed, oversized, length-mismatched or hash-invalid payloads fail closed; post-review identity drift returns changed. No Registry, Catalog, package, firmware parser, firmware executor, second timeout, second payload parser or payload cache is added.

designReview.evidence: Three independent read-only reviews of cf30c75a found the eager unbounded Bootstrap read and pre-budget admission to be a P1. They converged on pure host wiring, stream factories owned by the existing payload source, one Application entry budget, bounded descriptor and Bootstrap admission, lazy Setup hashing/capture, and tracking-stream plus monotonic-time regression evidence. The owner subsequently set the unified Launcher/Bootstrap executable safety ceiling to 200 MB without adding a package-size release gate.
